## Detailed Findings

#### 1. Kilocode session tab keyboard shortcuts SMALL ~2-3h (tools, TUI keybinds)

- **What**: Kilocode PR #14887 (merged 2026-10-07) adds keyboard shortcuts to switch session tabs. Commit title: "feat(vscode): switch session tabs with keyboard shortcuts". VSCode extension now supports Ctrl+PageUp (previous tab) and Ctrl+PageDown (next tab) to cycle through open session tabs without mouse. Kilocode session manager maintains tab order, keybind handler cycles index modulo tab count. Alexi TUI has session switching via command palette (Ctrl+K s) but no direct keyboard shortcuts for tab navigation. Adding Ctrl+PageUp/PageDown (or equivalent TUI-compatible keybinds like Ctrl+Shift+Left/Right) enables fast tab switching without opening palette.

- **Why**: Alexi CLI has `src/cli/tui/context/SessionContext.tsx` (session state), `src/cli/tui/context/KeybindContext.tsx` (keybind registry), and `src/cli/interactive.ts` L2457 (Tab key cycles agents when no completions). TUI session switching currently requires command palette or `ax sessions` command. Kilocode pattern: register Ctrl+PageUp/PageDown in keybind context, handler increments/decrements active session index modulo session count, updates SessionContext. Alexi equivalent: read active session list from SessionContext or SessionManager, compute next/previous session ID, call existing session switch handler (likely `switchSession` in SessionContext or interactive.ts). SMALL ~2-3h: register two keybinds in KeybindContext (Ctrl+PageUp → `previousSession`, Ctrl+PageDown → `nextSession`), implement handlers that read session list from SessionContext/SessionManager, compute wraparound index, call existing session switch logic, add test that keybind fires handler and session changes. Verify TUI session list shows active indicator after switch.

- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/14887 (session tab keyboard shortcuts), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/cli/tui/context/SessionContext.tsx (session state), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/cli/tui/context/KeybindContext.tsx (keybind registry), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/cli/interactive.ts L2457 (Tab key agent cycling)

- **Category**: tools (TUI keybinds, session navigation)

- **Size**: SMALL ~2-3h (register Ctrl+PageUp/PageDown in KeybindContext, implement previousSession/nextSession handlers, read session list from SessionContext/SessionManager, compute wraparound index, call existing session switch logic, add unit test keybind fires and session changes, verify TUI session list updates active indicator)

#### 2. Kilocode worktree pinning in Agent Manager sidebar MEDIUM ~4-6h (tools, Agent Manager)

Commit titles: "feat(agent-manager): pin worktrees in the sidebar", "Allow pinning worktrees with Shift+click or the context menu. Pinned worktrees lead the sidebar above ungrouped worktrees and sections, and keep their section so unpinning returns them to it.", "fix(agent-manager): keep the pin on no-op section moves". Users Shift+click a worktree or use context menu "Pin" to pin it. MEDIUM ~4-6h: extend WorktreeStatusEntry type, implement sort logic, add Shift+click handler to Sidebar or WorktreesSection, wire to orchestration API toggleWorktreePin, persist pin state, add unit tests (pin/unpin updates state, sort order correct, persistence roundtrips), verify TUI renders pinned worktrees at top with indicator.

#### 3. Kilocode MCP OAuth re-authorization at new authorization server MEDIUM ~6-8h (mcp, OAuth)

- **What**: Kilocode commit (merged 2026-10-07, exact PR number not in top 20 but referenced in commit message scan) adds "fix(cli): let configured MCP OAuth clients re-authorize at a new authorization server". MCP servers using OAuth (e.g. GitHub, Gitlab, Slack connectors) can now re-authorize when the token endpoint URL changes (e.g. migrating from `tenant-a.example.com/oauth/token` to `tenant-b.example.com/oauth/token`). Before: MCP client stored `refreshToken` + `tokenEndpoint` + `clientId` + `clientSecret` in connector store (`~/.kilo/mcp-connectors.json` or similar), refresh flow sent `refreshToken` to stored `tokenEndpoint`, but if authorization server URL changed (tenant migration, new OAuth provider), refresh failed with 401 and user had to manually delete connector entry + re-authorize from scratch. After: MCP client detects authorization server change (new `tokenEndpoint` in config vs stored `tokenEndpoint`), invalidates stored tokens, triggers fresh OAuth authorization flow, persists new `tokenEndpoint` + tokens. Alexi has MCP client (`src/mcp/client.ts` 2102 lines), connector store (`src/providers/connectorStore.ts` with `tokenEndpoint`, `refreshToken`, `clientId`, `clientSecret` fields per entry), OAuth refresh flow in `src/providers/auth.ts` (`refreshAccessToken` L324). No evidence of authorization server change detection or re-authorization flow.

- **Why**: Alexi MCP config lives in `mcp-servers.json` (per `src/mcp/config.ts` `loadMcpConfig`). Connector store (`src/providers/connectorStore.ts` L54 `tokenEndpoint`, L50 `refreshToken`, L56 `clientId`, L58 `clientSecret`) persists OAuth credentials. `src/providers/auth.ts` L324 `refreshAccessToken` function already implements OAuth 2.0 refresh flow (sends `refresh_token` grant to token endpoint, handles 4xx as `ReauthenticationRequiredError`). Missing piece: detection of authorization server change (config `tokenEndpoint` ≠ stored `tokenEndpoint`) + invalidation of stored tokens + re-authorization trigger. Kilocode pattern: (1) before refresh, compare config `tokenEndpoint` with stored `tokenEndpoint`, (2) if mismatch, invalidate stored tokens (set `accessToken`/`refreshToken` to `undefined`), (3) throw `ReauthenticationRequiredError` so caller triggers fresh OAuth authorization, (4) persist new `tokenEndpoint` with new tokens after authorization. Alexi equivalent: (1) audit `src/mcp/client.ts` MCP server connect flow for OAuth-backed servers (likely calls `src/providers/auth.ts` `refreshAccessToken` or reads connector store directly), (2) add authorization server change detection before refresh (read config `tokenEndpoint`, read stored connector entry `tokenEndpoint`, compare), (3) if mismatch, invalidate stored tokens + throw `ReauthenticationRequiredError`, (4) wire re-authorization flow (likely exists for initial OAuth authorization, reuse that path), (5) persist new `tokenEndpoint` to connector store after successful authorization. MEDIUM ~6-8h: audit MCP OAuth flow in `src/mcp/client.ts` (find connect path for OAuth servers, identify refresh call site), add authorization server mismatch detection (compare config vs stored `tokenEndpoint`), invalidate tokens on mismatch, throw `ReauthenticationRequiredError`, wire to existing OAuth authorization flow (check `src/mcp/auth-failure.ts` or `src/providers/auth.ts` for authorization trigger), persist new `tokenEndpoint` to connector store, add unit tests (mismatch detected, tokens invalidated, re-auth triggered, new endpoint persisted), add integration test (mock OAuth server, change endpoint URL, verify re-authorization succeeds).

- **Source**: Kilocode commit message "fix(cli): let configured MCP OAuth clients re-authorize at a new authorization server" (merged 2026-10-07, exact PR number not in top 20 commits but visible in commit scan), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/mcp/client.ts (MCP client, 2102 lines), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/providers/connectorStore.ts L54 (tokenEndpoint), L50 (refreshToken), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/providers/auth.ts L324 (refreshAccessToken OAuth flow), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/mcp/config.ts (loadMcpConfig)

- **Category**: mcp (OAuth re-authorization, authorization server change detection)

- **Size**: MEDIUM ~6-8h (audit MCP OAuth flow in client.ts, add authorization server mismatch detection before refresh, invalidate stored tokens on mismatch, throw ReauthenticationRequiredError, wire to existing OAuth authorization flow, persist new tokenEndpoint to connector store, add unit tests mismatch/invalidation/re-auth/persistence, add integration test mock OAuth server endpoint change)

Commit title: "chore(llms): align the AI SDK on one release line (ai 7.0.120, provider-utils 5.0.50)". REFERENCE-ONLY: Cline pattern shows importance of aligning transitive dependency versions when multiple packages share a peer (provider-utils in their case). If Alexi ever adopts AI SDK for multi-provider support (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google via `@ai-sdk/*` adapters), remember to pin all packages to same provider-utils version. No immediate work required - Alexi does not use AI SDK.
